title: Custom Input Devices for Cooperative Gaming
description: Built and evaluated separate physical controllers for cooperative gameplay, comparing them with a shared keyboard in Fireboy and Watergirl.

sections.title: Research question
sections.text: How does physically separating the controls affect performance and the user experience when two people play together?

sections.title: Prototype & study
sections.text: The team built custom USB input devices using cardboard, copper tape and keyboard membranes. An existing game, Fireboy and Watergirl, provided the task. Twelve people participated; ten were included in the analysis after two participants encountered technical problems.

sections.title: Evaluation
sections.text: The study compared a shared keyboard with separate custom input devices, using attempts, level completion time, SUS questionnaires and interviews. Statistical data analysis was carried out by other team members.

sections.title: Findings & limitations
sections.text: The prototype group required more attempts. No statistically significant difference was detected in SUS scores or completion time. Interview feedback highlighted the appeal of separated controls, alongside improvements needed in ergonomics and hardware reliability. The small sample and technical issues limit the conclusions.

sections.title: My contribution
sections.text: I contributed to controller prototyping and USB integration, study design, participant testing and report writing. I did not carry out the statistical data analysis.
